clue.text: Quiet priest receiving second element of transfusion

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for playing quietly

indicators.note: the priest takes in, or receives, the letter for second within himself

parts.note: a lama is a Buddhist priest in Tibet

explanation.surface: A hushed cleric is given a blood product during a hospital transfusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is the liquid part of blood, often given on its own in transfusions.

clue.text: Rise to receive actor finally in shows where children are entertained

indicators.note: the rising phrase with its extra letter sits inside the word for shows

parts.note: plays are stage shows

indicators.note: the phrase for rising opens up to take in the next letter

parts.note: to go up is to rise

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word actor

explanation.surface: A performer's late arrival lifts the theatre shows put on for youngsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Playgroups are informal preschool sessions where small children play together under supervision.

clue.text: Shellfish intrigue, not having caught single specimen

indicators.note: the plot word goes without the letter for caught

parts.note: a cabal is a secret plot or the group hatching it
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
one is a single example or specimen

explanation.surface: A conspiracy around shellfish lacks even one caught example.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail prized for its mother-of-pearl shell.

clue.text: I'm not safe broadcasting political statement

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters something widely, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician worries that airing a policy document will leave them exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a party's published declaration of its policies and aims.

clue.text: Brewing beer's out, I admit

indicators.note: brewing stirs and works ingredients together, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A publican confesses that the home-brewed beer has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish-flavoured phrase is a conversational concession, like saying certainly or admittedly.

clue.text: Witness possibly going over side of road mostly

indicators.note: in a down entry this piece sits above, or over, the next one

parts.note: someone on the loo is possibly going to the toilet, a jokey euphemism

indicators.note: mostly means dropping the final letter of the word for the roadside

parts.note: a kerb is the edge of a road or pavement

explanation.surface: A bystander may be crossing over the edge of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly going' is humorous: ON LOO, someone who may be going. 'over' places it above KER, which is KERB with 'mostly' cutting its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker is a bystander who watches an event, as a witness to it does.

clue.text: Husband low in courage finding hideaway

indicators.note: the husband letter is placed low down in the word for courage, at its bottom end

parts.note: heart means courage or spirit

explanation.surface: A man lacking nerve finds somewhere to hide away.
explanation.definitionFit: An earth is the underground den where a fox or badger hides.

clue.text: Madden crazed Hun in, say, uprising

indicators.note: crazed means wildly disordered, so these letters are scrambled
in a down entry, rising means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for say, meaning for example

explanation.surface: A frenzied invader in a revolt drives everyone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazed' rearranges HUN IN to UNHIN; 'uprising' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhinge someone is to unsettle their mind, to drive them mad.

clue.text: Bring in a lot of water for the French sailors

indicators.note: a lot of the word, not all of it, so its last letter goes

parts.note: eau is French for water
RN is the Royal Navy, hence sailors

explanation.surface: French sailors bring aboard plenty of water.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn money is to bring it in as income.

clue.text: Leading performer nude? Not half

indicators.note: not the whole word, only its first half is kept

parts.note: starkers is British slang for stark naked

explanation.surface: Asked whether the headline act appears naked, the reply is a cheeky British 'not half!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is also British slang for 'very much so', which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is the principal performer or lead in a show.

clue.text: Not favouring range this month

parts.note: an Aga is a brand of kitchen range cooker
inst., short for instant, is old letter-writing shorthand for this month

explanation.surface: Someone opposes buying a new cooker this month.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is a British range cooker brand; 'inst.' means 'of this month' in old business letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be against something is to oppose it, the opposite of favouring it.

clue.text: Dog walking is awkward for such a person

definitions.meaning: a crossbred hunting dog, part greyhound

definitions.text: walking is awkward for such a person
definitions.meaning: someone who staggers or lurches along walks unsteadily

explanation.surface: A dog's owner finds walks awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a crossbred dog and, cryptically, one who staggers or sways.

clue.text: Someone paid to commit crime?

parts.note: a person who must be paid to do wrong behaves well without any fee, so is good for no payment at all

explanation.surface: A hired criminal, a hitman perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer literally: the person behaves well, is good, for nothing, unless money is offered for wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual sense is a useless idler, but the clue reads it as being virtuous without payment.

clue.text: Our son is mistakenly following church, making moral judgments?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come after, or follow, the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: mistakenly means wrongly put together, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A parent laments that their son wrongly follows the church and judges everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' signals the anagram of OUR SON IS; 'following' puts that after the church abbreviation. The question mark flags a slightly loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Censorious means severely critical, given to passing moral judgment on others.

clue.text: Statement that threatens source of wealth given to London college

parts.note: ore is mined rock from which valuable metal is extracted
LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A donor's mineral fortune is handed to a London college with a warning attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Or else is said as a threat of consequences if something is not done.

clue.text: Example of chivalry to occur with distinction, not involving Society

parts.note: to be is to exist or occur

indicators.note: the word for distinct leaves out the letter for Society

parts.note: diverse means distinct or differing from one another

explanation.surface: Chivalry happens with honour, without high society involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedivere was one of King Arthur's knights, an embodiment of chivalry.

clue.text: Popular artist with show perhaps neglecting former restraint

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the exhibitor word leaves out, or neglects, the letters for former

parts.note: an exhibitor is someone showing work, for example an artist with an exhibition
ex means former

explanation.surface: A well-liked artist stages a show, setting aside an old restriction.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhibitor is something that holds back or checks a process, a restraint on it.

clue.text: Urine not affected? This barely affects anything

indicators.note: affected means altered, so these letters are changed in order

explanation.surface: A medical test reports that urine shows no change.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutrinos are particles that pass through matter almost without interacting with it.

clue.text: Angelic figure leading plot is ready for publication

parts.note: a putto is a cherubic infant figure in Renaissance art
a bed is a garden plot for plants

explanation.surface: A cherub heads a story that is finally ready to print.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is put to bed when it is finalised and sent for printing.

clue.text: Goes initially to English port

parts.note: has a go means tries, so goes is tries

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of to

explanation.surface: A traveller first makes for an English harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a major seaport in north-eastern Italy on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Current topic involving a hint of temptation to wit

indicators.note: the topic word wraps around, so involves, the other letters

parts.note: this can denote the matter currently under discussion

indicators.note: a hint of gives just the first letter of temptation

explanation.surface: Today's subject touches lightly on temptation, namely.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce a clarification, meaning namely.

clue.text: Physician's proverbial target: beginning to treat fleshy spread

indicators.note: beginning to selects the first letter of treat
spread means splayed out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor's goal is starting treatment for a flabby, spreading waistline.
explanation.walkthrough: From the proverb 'Physician, heal thyself'. 'spread' is the anagram signal and 'beginning to' takes the first letter of 'treat'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying tells the doctor to cure himself, so the reflexive pronoun is the physician's target.

clue.text: Someone no longer at home in the world of letters?

definitions.text: Someone no longer at home in the world of letters?

parts.words: Someone no longer at home in the world of letters?
parts.note: a person who stops renting from landlords, those who let property, and buys a house of their own

explanation.surface: A writer who no longer feels comfortable in literary circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' here means landlords who let, not literature: buying a first home leaves the renting world.
explanation.definitionFit: This buyer is purchasing property for the first time, typically leaving rented accommodation.

clue.text: Satirist's investigation about women

indicators.note: the investigation word goes about, surrounding, the women letter

parts.note: a sift is a careful sorting or examination

explanation.surface: A satirical writer's inquiry concerns women.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels and A Modest Proposal, classics of satire.

clue.text: Epigram including nothing debatable

indicators.note: the saying takes in the round letter

parts.note: a mot, as in bon mot, is a witty saying
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A witty saying with no content is open to argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot point is one that is open to discussion and unresolved.

clue.text: TV programme upset about soldiers in country

indicators.note: the upturned programme goes about the soldiers
in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so read the letters upwards

parts.note: QI is a British television quiz show
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: A TV show is upset about troops being deployed abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: QI is a long-running BBC panel quiz show.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a nation in the Middle East.

clue.text: Stood, mostly taking offence with one opera producer

indicators.note: mostly drops the last letter of the word for stood

parts.note: rose means stood up
a sin is a moral offence
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone rose to their feet, mostly offended, during an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini composed operas including The Barber of Seville, so produced them.

clue.text: Active period of time suppressing male self-importance

indicators.note: the period of time suppresses, squashes out, the letter for male

parts.note: a month is a period of time
ego is an inflated sense of one's own importance

explanation.surface: A busy spell keeps a man's vanity in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period of time' tempts with TERM or ERA; it is MONTH, with 'suppressing' removing M.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the go means being busy and constantly active.

clue.text: Poser: fools recalled nothing internally after quite ignoring it

indicators.note: the fools part comes after the shortened quite
the word quite ignores, leaves out, the letters of it
the round letter goes inside the reversed fools
recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: nits are fools or idiots
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A puzzle: idiots remember nothing inside after leaving quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns the fools backwards to STIN; 'internally' gives STION; 'after' sets that behind the trimmed 'quite', from which 'ignoring it' drops IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question.

clue.text: Hair laid back for one amongst cats where there are lots of dogs

definitions.text: where there are lots of dogs

indicators.note: the reversed hair goes in place of the letter standing for one in the word cats

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: laid back means turned to lie backwards, so the letters reverse

parts.note: fur is animal hair

explanation.surface: Fur lies flat on one cat among many where the dogs are.
explanation.walkthrough: A is one; RUF replaces it in CATS. CRUFTS is Britain's famous annual dog show.
explanation.definitionFit: Crufts is the large dog show in Birmingham, attracting thousands of dogs.
